docs.title: Bash CLI skeleton (bash-cli)
docs.text: A standalone Bash CLI starter (templates/bash-cli/, bin/scaffold/bash_cli.sh). This is the skeleton publishprobe (greenfield#26) is scaffolded from.

docs.title: What it ships
docs.text:
• bin/<project-name> — entrypoint with --version/--help, a CLI_VERSION="0.0.0" stub (stamped at install/release time, never hand-bumped).
  • lib/common.sh — the same print_status implementation every BlueprintX skeleton ships (templates/common/bin/lib/common.sh), copied verbatim.
  • tests/cli.bats — bats coverage for --version/--help/an unknown command.
  • Makefile — lint (shellcheck + shfmt), test (bats), install.
  • .github/workflows/ci.yml — lint + test jobs, each with timeout-minutes.
  • .github/workflows/release.yml, .pre-commit-config.yaml, .gitignore, README.md, AGENTS.md (with a CLAUDE.md shim that imports it).

docs.title: Versioning — mirrors how BlueprintX releases itself
docs.text:
The version is the git tag, never a hand-bump:

  • From a git checkout → bin/<name> runs git describe --tags --always at runtime, exactly like bin/blueprintx.sh's own print_version.
  • From make install (no .git at the install destination) → the recipe stamps the clone's current git describe into the installed entrypoint's CLI_VERSION literal via sed, mirroring the root Makefile's install target.
  • From a Release → .github/workflows/release.yml is BlueprintX's own release.yml orchestrator trimmed to the one channel v1 ships: a tag job (workflow_dispatch → version input, creates + pushes vX.Y.Z) followed by a github_release job that stamps that version into the tarball's entrypoint the same way, then publishes a GitHub Release with the tarball + a .sha256 checksum.

docs.title: Deferred release channels (backlog)
docs.text: BlueprintX itself also ships Homebrew, apt (gh-pages), Snap, and (optional) Chocolatey sub-workflows (.github/workflows/release_*.yml) called from its release.yml orchestrator. This skeleton's v1 ships only the GitHub Release + make install leg — start small, verify the skeleton scaffolds/lints/tests green first. Adding the remaining channels as release_*.yml sub-workflows (same workflow_call + needs: tag pattern) is tracked in .specs/backlog/bash-cli-skeleton_20260917_171817.md.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text: Dry-run coverage: bash-cli is in dry-run-smoke's matrix (.github/workflows/scaffold_checks.yml) — bin/blueprintx.sh new --dry-run exercises the skeleton via templates/*/skeleton.meta discovery, no code change needed there. A real scaffold + make lint + make test run is not yet wired into scaffold-lint-test (that matrix is Python-only, driven by bin/ci/scaffold_lint_test.sh, which is Poetry/pytest-specific and owned by a sibling issue, #481) — verified manually for this PR instead (see PR description).

docs.title: Etcher ChromeOS flasher skeleton (etcher-chromeos)
docs.text: A Bash CLI starter (templates/etcher-chromeos/, bin/scaffold/etcher_chromeos.sh) that rebuilds a ChromeOS-family pendrive. It follows the bash-cli skeleton and adds a flash command. The image defines the partition layout (12 partitions on a ChromeOS drive), so the tool selects, downloads, verifies and flashes; it never builds partitions.

docs.title: What it ships
docs.text:
• bin/<project-name> flash asks for the pendrive path first (--target skips the prompt), then the OS (--os chromeos-flex|fydeos, default from the default_os answer).
  • lib/device.sh resolves the path to the whole disk and refuses a device that is not removable or has mounted partitions. A flash shows model, size and partitions and requires typing the device name (--confirm answers it non-interactively).
  • lib/flex.sh, lib/fydeos.sh, lib/flash.sh, lib/verify.sh.
  • bin/fetch_tools.sh (make tools, make tools_etcher) fills a git-ignored .tools/.
  • Dockerfile for tests and resolvers only, tests/cli.bats with fixtures.

docs.title: Research findings
docs.text:
ChromeOS Flex. Google publishes https://dl.google.com/dl/edgedl/chromeos/recovery/cloudready_recovery2.json, a list of entries per channel (STABLE, BETA, DEV, LTC, LTR). Each carries url (a zip), zipfilesize, file, filesize, and the sha1 and md5 of the unzipped .bin. The CLI picks the highest version of the requested channel, checks the zip size, unzips, then checks the image size and SHA-1. The image is about 9.5 GB, so it needs a 16 GB or larger pendrive; a smaller device is refused before any write.

FydeOS. The download page publishes a SHA-256 per variant (for example FydeOS_for_PC_v19.0-io-stable.img.xz and FydeOS_for_PC_iris_v23.0-SP1-io.bin.zip) but the links are chosen on a rendered page, with no unauthenticated "latest" URL or machine readable index. The CLI therefore takes a file you downloaded plus its published SHA-256 (--file, --sha256) and verifies the archive before unpacking .img.xz or .zip.

Flashing. balenaEtcher 2.x has no maintained CLI and ships no AppImage (a zip and .deb/.rpm). The CLI writes with bmaptool copy --nobmap when it is available, else dd conv=fsync status=progress. make tools_etcher fetches the GUI, verified against Etcher's SHA256SUMS.Linux.x64.txt, for hand use.

Trust model for tools. Whatever runs as root against a block device must be publisher-attested, so bmaptool is never downloaded. make tools uses command -v bmaptool (a distro-signed package: apt install bmap-tools, dnf install bmap-tools) and otherwise leaves flashing to plain dd. bmaptool's GitHub releases carry no assets and no checksum, so there is nothing to verify a download against. The balenaEtcher GUI is the only download, opt-in (make tools_etcher ALLOW_UNSIGNED_DOWNLOAD=1 or --allow-github-digest), with a warning: it is protected only by Etcher's SHA256SUMS.Linux.x64.txt from the same release, which detects corruption, not a tampered release. Nothing is pinned: the latest release is resolved at run time, the tag must match ^v?[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)*$ and asset names ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ before a URL is built, the download works in a temporary directory removed on exit, the checksum line must match the filename exactly, and curl is restricted to HTTPS with TLS 1.2 or later.

docs.title: Docker
docs.text: Writing a device from a container needs --privileged or --device and loses the removable-device check, so it is not supported. The Dockerfile runs the bats suite only.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text: tests/cli.bats stubs curl, lsblk, dd and sync on PATH. It covers manifest parsing against a fixture, a checksum mismatch, a non-removable device, a mounted device, an unconfirmed device, an undersized device and both FydeOS hash outcomes.

docs.title: Ventoy USB skeleton (ventoy-usb)
docs.text: Generates a repo that rebuilds a Ventoy multiboot drive with a fixed folder layout, downloading the payload at build time. Nothing is copied from an existing drive and no ISO, installer or persistence image is committed (.gitignore excludes *.iso *.exe *.zip *.dat *.7z, build/ and .tools/). The repo plus the manifest replaces a ~50 GB backup of the drive. Source: templates/ventoy-usb/, bin/scaffold/ventoy_usb.sh (blueprintx#817, parent #816).

docs.title: What it ships
docs.text:
• sources.manifest: one line per payload (id|group|folder|kind|source|pattern|checksum|persist|extract|trust). The drive tree, the downloads and ventoy/ventoy.json are all derived from it.
  • bin/<project>: layout, tools, fetch, persistence, config, check, build, drive.
  • lib/: manifest.sh (parse and validate), resolve.sh (resolvers, download, verify), layout.sh, ventoy_config.sh (ventoy.json, persistence image), drive.sh (device guard).
  • ventoy-usb.conf: the scaffold answers (INCLUDE_WINDOWS, INCLUDE_ANDROID, PERSISTENCE_SIZE_MB).
  • payload/: files copied verbatim onto the tree (owner scripts, small PDFs).
  • tests/*.bats: layout diff, manifest parsing, resolvers, ventoy.json path check, device guard. Network is stubbed through CURL=tests/helpers/curl_stub.sh.

docs.title: Resolvers
docs.text:
No version is ever pinned: each entry resolves the newest upstream version at run time, and an entry that cannot be resolved fails alone with a message while the rest continue.

kind newest version comes from checksum dirsums the newest name matching pattern in a published checksum file (GNU, BSD and multi-section formats) the same file github latest release asset the asset digest the GitHub API reports dirindex newest link matching pattern in an HTML directory index sidecar:<suffix> file sfrss SourceForge file feed (rss?path=, 100 newest items) sidecar, or the md5 in the feed archive archive.org item metadata the sha1 in the metadata latesturl a vendor URL that always serves the latest installer none published; re-downloaded when Content-Length changes windows Microsoft's software-download-connector API (the Fido/Mido flow): a fresh time-limited link per run none via the API manual nothing resolvable n/a

A missing or unparsable checksum fails the entry (fail closed). The only opt-out is an explicit none:<reason>, allowed for github (an asset with no API digest), dirindex, latesturl and windows; dirsums, sfrss and archive always carry a checksum. Hashes are matched by length (sha256, sha1, md5); md5 and sha1 come from the upstream's own feed and are weaker.

Measured 2026-10-16 (every kind returned its entry live except Windows, which Microsoft rejected, and Clonezilla, whose mirror was down):

Source Kind Newest comes from Ubuntu desktop and server 24.04.x, Lubuntu 26.04.x, Kali, Rocky 10, Proxmox VE, Clonezilla, KolibriOS dirsums checksum file listing Talos, MiniOS, Ventoy, Rufus, RustDesk github latest release TrueNAS SCALE dirindex root index, stable releases of any train SystemRescue, Android-x86, PrimeOS, Lineage x86 TV (lineageos-tv-x86) sfrss SourceForge feed tiny11 archive the maintainer's tiny11_latest item AnyDesk, Firefox, Office, Power BI, Revo (and portable) latesturl vendor URL Windows 11 pt-BR windows Microsoft API HDT manual unmaintained, no feed

Series that are part of an upstream path (Ubuntu 24.04, Lubuntu 26.04, Rocky 10) are the release line the drive tracks, not a pinned point release.

Windows 11: Microsoft's API sometimes answers Sentinel marked this request as rejected. That is a per-entry failure with a message to download the ISO into payload/isos/Windows/. The API publishes no SHA-256, so the entry carries an explicit none:<reason>; TLS to microsoft.com is the only integrity check.

A github digest is computed by GitHub: it detects corruption or a swapped download, not a compromised publisher.

docs.title: Persistence and ventoy.json
docs.text:
Ventoy publishes prebuilt persistence images in the ventoy/backend releases (images.zip holding persistence_ext4_<N>GB_<label>.dat.7z; the release notes list their sha256). The build downloads the one matching the configured size and label, verifies the 7z against the release notes and extracts it. Only when no published image matches (for example a size that is not 1, 2 or 4 GB) does it fall back to Ventoy's CreatePersistentImg.sh -s <MB> -t ext4 -l <label> -o <path>, which needs root for a loop device.

The release the image came from is recorded in persistance/.persistence-release. When a newer ventoy/backend release exists, both build and the drive sync replace the image by default and print a warning that its saved session data is lost; --keep-persistence (or KEEP_PERSISTENCE=1 with make) opts out. A changed size or label always yields a new image, and an unreachable ventoy/backend keeps the existing one. The folder is spelled persistance, as on the original drive.

ventoy.json is generated from the manifest, so a persistence image is the path the ISO actually landed at (/isos/Linux/Desktop/ubuntu-...iso). check, also run by build, fails if any absolute path in the file is missing from the tree. The drive this was measured from had exactly that defect.

docs.title: Trust levels
docs.text:
Each manifest entry names how its download is authenticated, and the build prints the level.

level meaning entries gpg:<fingerprint>:<suffix>:<key url> the checksum file's detached signature is verified with gpg against a key whose 40-hex fingerprint is written in the manifest (the key file must hold exactly that one key, the signature must be detached and good, and the primary fingerprint of the signer must match); a missing gpg, key or valid signature fails the entry Ubuntu desktop and server, Lubuntu (Ubuntu CD signing key), Kali two-origin the GitHub digest must equal the sha256 listed on ventoy.net; a disagreement fails, and so does an unreachable second origin unless ALLOW_SINGLE_ORIGIN=1 is set (then it warns) Ventoy same-origin-digest the checksum comes from the same place as the file: it detects corruption, not a tampered upstream the other checksum-bearing entries (Rocky, Proxmox, Clonezilla, KolibriOS, TrueNAS, SystemRescue, MiniOS, Talos, Rufus, RustDesk, SourceForge and archive.org entries, the persistence image) none the vendor publishes nothing; explicit none:<reason> in the checksum field vendor installers, Windows 11

Rocky's CHECKSUM and Proxmox's and Clonezilla's checksum files have no signature or key I could verify here, so they stay same-origin-digest. Ventoy2Disk runs as root on a block device, so the tarball's two-origin check matters most.

Test hooks (CURL, GITHUB_API, LSBLK, FINDMNT, VENTOY_DIR, DRIVE_MNT, SUDO) are ignored unless VENTOY_USB_TESTING=1, so the environment cannot redirect a root-run tool.

Hardening: every request uses --proto =https --tlsv1.2; names taken from upstream must match ^[A-Za-z0-9._+-]+$ without .., and a GitHub download URL must be on github.com; archives extract into a fresh temp dir; the sync deletes a symlink on the drive as the link itself, never follows it, and runs rm --one-file-system; checksum lines are matched exactly.

docs.title: Tools
docs.text: make tools (also run when Ventoy is missing) downloads the latest Ventoy Linux release into the git-ignored .tools/ and verifies the sha256 GitHub publishes for it.

docs.title: Writing a drive
docs.text:
make drive asks for the pendrive path (or takes TARGET=), resolves it to the block device and refuses anything lsblk does not report as a removable disk (TYPE=disk RM=1).

  • Ventoy present (a VTOYEFI partition): sync. New and changed files are copied; an older version of a manifest entry is deleted automatically once the newer one is in place; every other item outside the layout asks delete <path>? [y/N] (default no, YES_DELETE_EXTRAS=1 answers yes to all).
  • Ventoy absent: install. Warns that the whole device is erased, shows model, size and partitions, requires the device name to be typed, runs Ventoy2Disk.sh -I, then syncs.

Both paths are tested with stubbed lsblk, findmnt and Ventoy2Disk.sh; no test touches a device. Docker is deliberately not used for this path: it needs --privileged or --device, which breaks removable-device detection and the partition re-read, and Ventoy has no official image.

docs.title: Payload
docs.text: Anything under payload/ is copied verbatim onto the tree (owner scripts, small PDFs). .gitignore excludes *.iso *.exe *.zip *.dat *.7z, not *.pdf, so keep a repo that commits third-party PDFs private.
